**Finding submitted: deviation (LD), fallback cure.**

- **Responsive clause:** Section 4.2 (p0025–p0029). Section 4.2(a) requires the Company to pay HDI a stipulated "Termination Payment" on any Company termination, equal to (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2 — a Customer-payable liquidated amount untethered to fees and capable of vastly exceeding three months' Section 3.1 fees. This fails the LD fallback cap.
- **Other locations checked:** Section 1.6 (limited penalty-free exit for a late Site launch — benefits us, not flagged), Section 3 fees/payment (no stipulated sums or minimum fees), Sections 4.2(b)–(c) (zero-value and eight quarterly instalment mechanics — machinery only, no cure), and the general provisions (no penalty or damages schedule). No LDs run from HDI to us.
- **Cure chosen:** fallback rather than preferred deletion, because removing the payment entirely would require collateral rewrites of the 4.2(b) zero-value provision, the 4.2(c) instalment mechanic, and the Section 4 heading. One surgical replacement caps the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees and makes it our sole early-termination fee and sole liquidated amount; all surrounding text is preserved verbatim and the retained 4.2(b)–(c) machinery still operates against the capped amount.
